title: Engineering Mindset
learn: Think in terms of problems, causes, requirements, solutions, testing, and improvement.
exercise: Choose one small problem you see around your home or community.
Write down exactly what the problem is.
Choose one solution and explain why.
mamelodi: Observe one practical problem in your community without trying to solve it immediately.
mmk: Choose one MMK problem, such as stock tracking, customer orders, digital services, or clothing sales. Define the problem clearly.
reflection: What did I learn about defining a problem before building a solution?

title: Observation
learn: Good engineering starts with careful observation instead of assumptions.
exercise: Write down each step you see.
Identify where time, money, materials, or effort are being wasted.
mamelodi: Observe how a local shop, salon, street vendor, or service handles customers.
mmk: Observe one MMK workflow from customer request to delivery and record every step.
reflection: What did I notice that I normally overlook?

title: Requirements
learn: A solution needs clear requirements before development begins.
exercise: Choose a simple product or service.
Write five things it must do.
Write three things it must not do.
mamelodi: Think about what a useful local digital service would need to do for a small business.
mmk: Write five requirements for the MMK Stock & Profit Calculator.

title: Specifications
learn: Specifications turn general requirements into measurable details.
exercise: Turn each into a measurable specification.
Define what would count as passing a test.
mamelodi: Choose a practical service and define one measurable quality standard.
mmk: Define measurable specifications for the MMK calculator, including currency, stock quantity, selling price, cost price, revenue, and profit.
reflection: Which requirements became clearer after adding measurements?

title: Prototype
learn: A prototype is an early working version used to learn and discover problems.
exercise: Do not try to make it perfect.
Write down what worked and what failed.
mamelodi: Create a simple paper or phone-based prototype for a local problem.
mmk: Identify one MMK feature that can be prototyped quickly.
reflection: What did the prototype teach me?

title: Testing
learn: Testing checks whether a solution actually works under defined conditions.
mamelodi: Test a simple service or process three times and record the results.
mmk: Run a test on one MMK software feature and record expected versus actual results.
reflection: What did testing reveal that guessing could not?

title: Quality Control
learn: Quality means consistently meeting defined requirements and standards.
mamelodi: Inspect one everyday service or product and identify five quality factors.
mmk: Create a five-point quality checklist for an MMK digital product.
reflection: What does professional quality mean to me?

title: Documentation
learn: Documentation makes work understandable, repeatable, maintainable, and transferable.
exercise: Choose one task you know how to perform.
Write the steps from beginning to end.
Check whether another beginner could follow it.
mamelodi: Document a useful local process that another person could learn from.
mmk: Document one MMK Termux workflow with commands, expected results, and testing steps.
reflection: Could another person reproduce my work from my documentation?

title: Reliability
learn: A professional system should behave predictably and handle normal mistakes safely.
exercise: Choose a simple system or process.
List three things that could go wrong.
Design a response for each problem.
mamelodi: Think about what could go wrong in a local business service and how the owner could recover.
mmk: Test an MMK application with incorrect or unexpected input and document what happens.
reflection: How can I design systems that people can trust?

title: Engineering Project
learn: Engineering combines problem definition, observation, requirements, specifications, prototyping, testing, quality, and documentation.
mamelodi: Complete the project using a real small problem you can safely observe in your community.
mmk: Apply the complete engineering cycle to one small MMK software, digital-service, clothing, gallery, or business problem.
reflection: What engineering principle from Days 1–10 will I continue using?
